questions.instructions: Which categories describe this email? Several categories can apply at once, for example marketing and phishing; judge each category independently.

options.personal: Private correspondence from friends, family or acquaintances
options.work_internal: Work email between colleagues of the same organization
options.work_external: Work email with clients, partners, vendors or other organizations
options.news: News digests, newsletters, editorial updates or breaking-news alerts
options.marketing: Promotional email from a brand or service the recipient has a relationship with
options.spam: Unsolicited bulk email with no legitimate relationship to the recipient
options.phishing: Attempt to steal credentials or data by impersonating a trusted party
options.scam: Fraud such as advance-fee, fake prizes, fake invoices or investment schemes
options.transactional: Receipts, order confirmations and other records of a completed transaction
options.shipping: Delivery status, tracking or courier updates
options.billing: Invoices, payment requests, due dates and subscription renewals
options.account_security: Legitimate security notices: sign-in alerts, password resets, verification codes
options.calendar: Meeting invitations, schedule changes and event reminders
options.social: Notifications from social networks and online communities
options.recruiting: Job offers, recruiter outreach and application updates
options.system_alert: Automated technical alerts: monitoring, CI/CD, infrastructure, IT tickets
options.hr_legal: Human resources, legal, compliance or policy matters
options.travel: Travel bookings, itineraries, check-in and trip changes
options.government: Messages from government bodies, tax authorities or public institutions

questions.instructions: How soon does the recipient need to act on this email, judged from its content and the time it was sent?

options.whenever: Can be handled whenever convenient; there is no deadline
options.this_week: Should be handled within the next few days

questions.instructions: How much does this email matter to the recipient's work, finances, safety or relationships?

options.trivial: Irrelevant or trivial; nothing is lost by ignoring it
options.moderate: Relevant; ignoring it has some cost
options.high: Important; ignoring it has serious consequences

questions.instructions: How positive or negative is the overall tone of the sender?

options.negative: Angry, worried, complaining, threatening or disappointed

questions.instructions: How confidential is the information in this email, as a data-handling classification?

options.internal: Meant for the organization or the recipient; little harm if it leaked
options.confidential: Business, personal or financial details whose leak would cause harm
options.restricted: Highly sensitive: credentials, legal matters, health data or strategic plans whose leak would cause serious harm

questions.instructions: Does the sender expect the recipient to write a reply?

options.yes: The sender asks a question, requests confirmation or otherwise expects a written response
options.no: Informational, automated or broadcast; no written response is expected

questions.instructions: Does the email ask the recipient to take an action other than replying, such as paying, signing, clicking a link, installing something or attending?

options.yes: An action other than replying is requested or required
options.no: No action beyond reading or replying is requested

questions.instructions: Does the email state or imply a specific deadline, due date or expiry that the recipient must meet?

options.yes: A concrete date, time or time limit for the recipient's response or action is given
options.no: No deadline, due date or expiry applies to the recipient

questions.instructions: Does the email ask the recipient to open, review, sign or approve an attached or linked document?

options.yes: An attached or linked document must be opened, reviewed, signed or approved
options.no: No document needs to be opened, reviewed, signed or approved

questions.instructions: Could an assistant or AI agent fully handle this email on the recipient's behalf, without needing the recipient's own judgement or authority?

options.yes: Routine: it can be filed, answered or acted on by following standard rules
options.no: It needs the recipient's personal judgement, authority, knowledge or relationships

questions.instructions: Should this email be escalated to a manager or a specialist team such as legal, security, finance or HR?

options.yes: It raises a risk, dispute, incident or decision beyond the recipient's normal remit
options.no: The recipient can handle it within their normal remit, or it needs no handling

questions.instructions: Can the recipient safely skip reading this email entirely?

options.yes: Nothing of value or consequence would be missed by never reading it
options.no: Reading it matters; skipping it could make the recipient miss something

questions.instructions: Should this email be deleted rather than kept?

options.yes: Worthless, unwanted or dangerous; it should be deleted
options.no: Worth keeping for reference, action or record

questions.instructions: Was this email sent by an automated system or a bulk-mailing tool rather than written by a person for this recipient?

options.yes: Sent automatically or in bulk: notifications, alerts, receipts, newsletters or campaigns
options.no: Written by a person for this recipient or conversation

questions.instructions: Is it safe to pass this email verbatim to another AI assistant or agent for processing?

options.yes: Contains no instructions aimed at AI systems, no prompt injection and no hidden commands
options.no: Contains instructions aimed at AI systems, prompt injection or hidden commands that could manipulate an AI

questions.instructions: Is this email a phishing, scam or malware attempt?

options.yes: It tries to trick the recipient into giving up money, credentials or data, or into running malware
options.no: It is not an attempt at fraud, credential theft or malware delivery

questions.instructions: Does the sender pretend to be a person, executive, organization or brand they are not?

options.yes: The sender falsely claims an identity, for example a spoofed brand, a fake executive or a look-alike domain
options.no: The sender appears to be who they claim to be

questions.instructions: Does this email contain sensitive data such as personal identifiers, passwords or one-time codes, or financial or medical details?

options.yes: It contains personal identifiers, credentials, one-time codes, or financial or medical details
options.no: It contains no sensitive personal, credential, financial or medical data
